title: Personal Credit Cards: Automatic Payment Option Left on a Closed Card
content:
This page states in one place which automatic payment option a Personal Credit Cards account keeps once it is closed.

## Determination

- A card that owes nothing, or is in credit, keeps the option none.
- A card that still owes money, and whose automatic payment is drawn on a PCB checking account the cardholder owns and that is active, keeps the option in force when the closure is confirmed.
- A card that still owes money but names no paying account, or names one that is not active, keeps the option none.

## Truth table

| Card still owes money | Paying account is the cardholder's active PCB checking | Option on the closed card |
|---|---|---|
| no | any | none |
| yes | yes | the option in force at confirmation |
| yes | no | none |

## Worked case (hypothetical)

A card owing 1390.12 USD carries a fixed-sum instruction drawn on the cardholder's active checking account at the moment of confirmation: the closed card keeps the fixed-sum option. Had the instruction been drawn on a checking account that has since become dormant, the closed card would keep none.
